classes.name: Presidenta o Presidente y Vicepresidenta o Vicepresidente de la República
classes.note: Joint tickets (binomios) elected in one national constituency that includes voters abroad (Código art. 151). First round won with an absolute majority of valid votes, or with at least 40% and a lead of more than ten points; otherwise a runoff between the top two within 45 days (Constitution art. 143, Código art. 161). The president may dissolve the Assembly once in the first three years, and the Assembly may remove the president; either calls early presidential and legislative elections for the rest of the term (arts. 130, 148), as in 2023. Direct presidential elections go back to the nineteenth century; the series itemized here starts with the 1978-1979 return to civilian rule.

classes.name: Elección del Presidente por el Congreso o una Convención Nacional
classes.name_en: President chosen by Congress or a national convention
classes.note: In the republic's first decades, and again whenever a constituent convention or Congress installed a constitutional or interim president during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, the head of state was chosen by the assembly rather than by popular vote.
classes.disposition_reason: The votes survive only in the minutes of the conventions and congresses; no electoral authority publishes them, and no official series exists to load.

classes.name: Asamblea Nacional
classes.note: Unicameral (Constitution art. 118). Fifteen members in a national constituency, two per province or metropolitan district plus one per 200,000 people or fraction over 150,000 (provinces electing eight or more are split into two to four districts), and six for three overseas constituencies (Código art. 150); 151 seats in 2025. Closed lists with seats by the Webster method (divisors 1, 3, 5, 7) since the 2020 reform (Código arts. 160, 164); before it voters could choose candidates across lists.

classes.name: Congreso Nacional (Cámara Nacional de Representantes)
classes.note: Unicameral congress of national and provincial deputies under the 1978 and 1998 constitutions; provincial deputies were renewed at mid-term (1986, 1990, 1994) until 1998. Suspended in November 2007 by the Constituent Assembly and replaced by the National Assembly in 2009.

classes.name: Congreso (Senado y Cámara de Diputados)
classes.name_en: Congress (Senate and Chamber of Deputies), before 1972
classes.note: Congresses elected under the constitutions of 1830-1967, bicameral for most of the period with functional senators; the last sat until the 1970 self-coup and the 1972 military government.
classes.disposition_reason: No electoral authority publishes results for congressional elections before 1978; they survive in provincial returns, congressional records and the press.

classes.name: Asamblea Constituyente
classes.note: The National Constituent Assembly of 1997 (70 members) and the Constituent Assembly of 2007 (130 members: 24 national, 100 provincial and 6 abroad), convened by the referendums of 1997 and 15 April 2007. Earlier conventions (1830-1967) are not itemized. A constituent assembly was proposed again in the referendum of 16 November 2025 and rejected.

classes.locator: https://www.defensa.gob.ec/wp-content/uploads/downloads/2021/02/Constitucion-de-la-Republica-del-Ecuador_act_ene-2021.pdf (Arts. 105, 106: any elected authority, after the first and before the last year of the term; absolute majority of valid votes, or of voters for the president)
classes.note: Recall of any elected authority on a petition of 10% of the electorate (15% for the president), voted in the authority's constituency; the Código sets the procedure (arts. 199-202). Held for local authorities in scattered votes; none has reached a president.

classes.name: Consejo provincial
classes.note: Since 2009 the council is the prefect and vice prefect with the mayors (or councillors) of the cantons and representatives chosen from among the rural parish board presidents. Before 2009 provincial councillors were elected directly with the sectional elections (2000 and 2004, with partial renewals in 2002 and 2006).
classes.disposition_reason: Its members sit ex officio or are chosen from among parish board presidents, with no popular vote; the directly elected provincial councillors ended in 2009 and are kept in the note.

classes.name: Circunscripción territorial indígena, afroecuatoriana o montubia
classes.note: Parishes, cantons or provinces that are mostly indigenous or Afro-Ecuadorian may become territorial circumscriptions governed by their own institutions.
classes.disposition_reason: None has been constituted by consultation, and their authorities would follow community procedures rather than an election run by the CNE.

classes.name: Procesos de democracia interna y elecciones primarias
classes.note: Every candidacy must come from a primary or internal democratic process (art. 94), open or closed or through party organs (art. 348), within a fifteen-day window before registration (art. 345).
classes.disposition_reason: The parties run and count their own primaries; the CNE only supervises, assists on request, and appoints observers (Código art. 345), and publishes no results.

classes.name: Juezas y jueces de paz
classes.locator: https://www.defensa.gob.ec/wp-content/uploads/downloads/2021/02/Constitucion-de-la-Republica-del-Ecuador_act_ene-2021.pdf (Art. 189: elected by their community through a process run by the Judicature Council)
classes.note: The only judges chosen by election. Every other judge, including the Constitutional Court and the National Court of Justice, is appointed by the Judicature Council or by qualifying commissions through merit contests (arts. 170, 182-183, 434).
classes.disposition_reason: Communities choose them in assemblies the Judicature Council organizes; the CNE does not run the vote and no results are published.
